questions.q: Why does upserting on an External ID make repeated loads from the same source idempotent?
options: Because Upsert deletes the file after one successful run
Because running the same file again updates existing matches instead of creating duplicates
Because External ID fields expire after 24 hours
Because Data Loader caches the first run's results and skips the second run entirely
questions.explain: On a second run, rows that already matched an existing record update it rather than inserting a new one — so the same file can be loaded repeatedly without creating duplicates.

questions.q: A team needs to load 500 new Leads from a trade-show spreadsheet. Which tool fits best by default?
options: Data Loader, because every load should use the desktop app
The Data Import Wizard, since it's a simple, smaller job on a supported object
Neither — Leads can only be created one at a time in the UI
The Bulk API command line, since nothing smaller is supported
questions.explain: The Import Wizard is built for exactly this: a guided flow for a supported object, well under its 50,000-record cap.

questions.q: What does Update match on, and what happens to a row with no value in that field?
options: It matches on Email, and the row is skipped quietly
It matches on record ID, and the row fails outright
It matches on Name, and the row is inserted as new instead
It matches on whatever field is listed first in the CSV
questions.explain: Update matches purely on the Salesforce record ID. A row missing that ID has nothing to match against and fails — there's no fallback to name or another field.

A desktop client that talks to Salesforce via SOAP or Bulk API
A Salesforce report type for exporting dashboards
A Chrome extension for editing records inline
questions.explain: Data Loader is a client application you install on your machine, which communicates with Salesforce through its SOAP or Bulk APIs.

questions.q: A job needs to load 80,000 Contacts using a custom matching rule for duplicates. Why does this fall outside the wizard?
options: Both the record count and the matching requirement exceed what the wizard supports
Contacts cannot be imported through the wizard at all
The wizard only accepts matching rules for Leads
80,000 records is within the limit, but custom matching requires Data Loader regardless of volume
questions.explain: 80,000 exceeds the wizard's 50,000-record cap, and the wizard's duplicate prevention is limited to account name/site or contact/lead email — not a custom matching rule. Either reason alone would be enough; together they're a clear signal to use Data Loader.

questions.q: What does "Include all data" control on the export options screen?
options: Whether field history is included
Whether the export includes every object you have access to, versus just a chosen subset
Whether Chatter posts are exported
Whether the file is compressed before download
questions.explain: Checking Include all data exports everything for a full backup; deselecting it lets you choose specific objects, producing a smaller, faster export.

questions.q: What changes when you check "Permanently delete the selected records"?
options: Nothing — it's only a confirmation label with no functional effect
Deleted records skip the Recycle Bin entirely and become unrecoverable immediately
Deleted records are backed up automatically before removal
It converts the delete into a mass transfer instead
questions.explain: Leaving it unchecked sends deleted records to the Recycle Bin like a normal delete. Checking it skips the Recycle Bin entirely — those records cannot be recovered.

questions.q: A record was deleted 18 days ago and is needed back. Why won't the Recycle Bin help, and what's the realistic fallback?
options: The Recycle Bin would still have it; no fallback is needed
It's past the 15-day retention window, so the fallback is restoring from a data export or scheduled backup, if one exists from before the deletion
Mass Transfer Records can retrieve deleted records regardless of age
There is no possible recovery after any deletion, regardless of timing
questions.explain: 18 days exceeds the Recycle Bin's roughly 15-day window, so the record has likely been purged. The fallback is a data export or scheduled backup taken before the deletion — exactly why those exist as a second layer.

questions.q: What does "Enable serial mode for Bulk API" trade away, and why would an admin choose it?
options: It trades speed for avoiding database contention on objects with heavy automation
It disables Bulk API entirely while leaving the checkbox checked
It increases the per-batch record limit beyond 10,000
It has no practical effect and exists only for legacy compatibility
questions.explain: Serial mode processes batches one at a time instead of in parallel. It's slower, but it avoids the record-locking contention that parallel writes can cause on heavily automated objects.

questions.q: Where do you set up a scheduled export?
options: A separate Setup menu item called "Scheduled Backups"
The same Data Export page used for manual exports, via the Schedule Export button
Only through the command-line Data Loader interface
Through a report subscription
questions.explain: Schedule Export lives on the same Data Export Setup page as Export Now — just a different button leading to a similar options screen plus a frequency setting.

questions.q: After cleanup, rows for Acme Corp became character-for-character identical. What's the right next step?
options: Import both rows as separate Accounts to preserve history
Delete both rows since neither can be trusted anymore
Convert the Company field to a formula field
Let a duplicate rule catch the match at import/save time rather than importing both blindly
questions.explain: This is exactly the scenario duplicate rules exist for — catching the match and letting the configured action (block, alert, or report) decide what happens, instead of silently creating two records for one company.

questions.q: In a custom matching rule, why is MatchBlank almost always left set to FALSE?
options: Setting it to TRUE disables the entire rule
Otherwise two records with an empty value in that field would be treated as a match
FALSE is required for Fuzzy fields, but not for Exact fields
It controls whether the rule applies to Leads versus Contacts
questions.explain: With MatchBlank = FALSE, blank values on both records don't count as a match. Leaving it TRUE would flag any two records that both happen to have an empty field.

questions.q: Why do "Texas", "TX", and "texas " cause problems in a grouped report, even though each individual record is accurate?
options: They are treated as three or four unrelated string values instead of one state
Salesforce reports cannot group on text fields at all
Grouped reports require picklist fields to run at all
Trailing spaces cause the report to fail silently
questions.explain: A grouped report, a filter, and an exact matching rule all compare strings literally. Different spellings or casing of the same real value produce separate buckets.

questions.q: Which standard matching/duplicate rule pairs ship active in a brand-new org?
options: All three pairs (Account, Contact, Lead) are active by default
Only the Account pair is active by default
None of them — all three pairs exist but must be activated manually
Only the matching rules are active; the duplicate rules still need activation
questions.explain: The three standard pairs exist in every org but ship inactive. Both the matching rule and its duplicate rule must be activated before anything fires.

questions.q: An org has validation rules, duplicate rules, and State/Country Picklists active, but new data still looks inconsistent after six months. What's the most likely gap?
options: Validation rules and duplicate rules cannot be active in the same org
State/Country Picklists disable all other data quality tools automatically
The org needs to delete and recreate all picklist fields
No one is reviewing reports or tuning the rules on an ongoing basis — the features exist but lack an owner
questions.explain: Features alone decay in effectiveness without a recurring review rhythm — false positives go untuned, Duplicate Record Sets pile up unreviewed, and picklist values drift.

questions.q: Why is DUPLICATE_VALUE easy to confuse with the Duplicate Rules from earlier in the course?
options: They are actually the same mechanism, just named differently
DUPLICATE_VALUE only appears when a Duplicate Rule is deactivated
Both involve the word 'duplicate,' but DUPLICATE_VALUE is a hard Unique-field constraint, unrelated to Duplicate Rules
DUPLICATE_VALUE always means a Duplicate Rule needs to be created
questions.explain: DUPLICATE_VALUE comes from a field-level Unique constraint and fires on every insert regardless of Duplicate Rule configuration. The actual Duplicate Rule equivalent is DUPLICATE_DETECTED.

questions.q: Why did the first batch of Contacts fail with INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY?
options: The Contacts file was missing a required field
The Contact object does not support bulk loading
A validation rule blocked every Contact record
Accounts and Contacts were submitted in the same batch, so Contacts referenced Account Ids that didn't exist yet
questions.explain: Parent records (Accounts) need to be loaded and confirmed before child records (Contacts) that reference them — loading them together broke the lookup.

questions.q: What does an upsert operation do that a plain update does not?
options: It deletes any record that doesn't match the file
It inserts a new record when no match is found, instead of failing
It skips validation rules for faster loading
It only works on the Account object
questions.explain: Update fails when no matching record exists. Upsert inserts a new record in that case instead, which is why it's safe to re-run.
